answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-backed lantern identities: every trader carries a verifiable credential issued after real-world KYC, and new identities must wander the public market for a seasoning period with capped trade sizes before earning trust. Fake accounts then cannot spin up instantly and blend in. Sybil farms would need distinct credentials plus seasoning time per identity, so their pigment of legitimacy fades — the cost of a thousand fakes exceeds the cost of a few honest lanterns, and peer attestation of completed work reinforces the real ones.
